question: Which of the following is an example of non-volatile memory?
solution:
The correct answer is __**ROM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Read-only memory (ROM), EPROM (erasable programmable ROM) and EEPROM (electrically erasable programmable ROM), ferroelectric RAM, **most types of computer data storage devices (e.g. disc storage, hard disc drives, optical discs, floppy discs, and magnetic tape), and early computer storage methods like punched tape and cards are all examples of non-volatile memory.
 
• In computers and other electronic devices,** read-only memory (ROM)** is a type of **non-volatile memory**.
 
• After the memory device is manufactured, data saved in ROM cannot be electronically manipulated. Read-only memory, commonly known as firmware, is useful for storing software that is rarely modified during the life of the device.
 
• Plug-in cartridges containing ROM can be used to deploy software applications (such as video games) for programmable devices. 
 
• Non-volatile memory (NVM) is a type of computer memory that can preserve data even after the power is turned off.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Random-access memory (RAM) **is a type of computer memory that allows data to be read and written in any sequence and is commonly used to store working data and machine code. To connect the data lines to the designated store for reading or writing the entry, RAM contains multiplexing and demultiplexing hardware.
 
• The technique of building an integrated circuit by putting millions of MOS transistors onto a single chip is known as** very large-scale integration(VLSI)**.
